newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to lag Bunds on politics, supply.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to lag Bunds on politics, supply.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds would lag Bunds further on Tuesday as the prospect of new supply replaced fears over the fate of a senior government minister who allegedly had sex with under-age boys, dealers said.

The benchmark 10-year OLO yield fell to 5.88 percent in late Monday dealings from 5.97 late on Friday. But the spread over Bunds widened to 12 from 10 basis points as the Belgian franc weakened on fears Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo could be indicted on the allegations, which he has denied.
Reports that Belgium's high court had found some of the allegations without base came after the OLO market had closed.
It was unclear whether the high court report into the allegations, which Di Rupo has always denied, would completely exonerate the minister.
A parliamentary commission was due to meet at 1700 GMT to discuss whether the report warranted further action.
Dealers said, however, that with an exchange auction on Tuesday and monthly OLO auction next Monday the Belgian market was likely to continue to lag Germany's.
"People are still waiting to see what is going to happen to Di Rupo and if there will be a further correction," one trader said.
At the exchange auction, the OLO expiring in May 1997 can be exchanged against OLOs expiring in April 1999, December 2000, June 2002, October 2004 and May 2006.
The OLO lines to be auctioned next Monday were due to be announced sometime after 1700 GMT.
Dealers said that in the event parliament felt Di Rupo should still face charges, the 10-year spread could widen to around 15 or 16 basis points.
One said, however, heavy selling pressure was unlikely. "We saw even last week that domestics do not really want to sell. They've finished for the year," he said.
